config..github/workflows/ci.yml:
# The checks on this page, on every push and pull request.
# Not run on this page: the sessions run the same commands in the runner image.
name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - run: cargo fmt --check
      - run: cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
      - run: cargo test --locked
config.deny.toml:
# cargo-deny settings. Not run on this page: cargo-deny is not installed in the image.
# Each key is described at https://embarkstudios.github.io/cargo-deny/checks/cfg.html

[advisories]
# Fail on crates the RustSec database marks unmaintained or unsound,
# whether you depend on them directly or not.
unmaintained = "all"
unsound = "all"
yanked = "deny"

[licenses]
# Only these licences are accepted; any other fails the check.
allow = ["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]

[bans]
# `serde = "*"` in a Cargo.toml fails the check.
wildcards = "deny"
# Two versions of one crate in the build is reported, not refused.
multiple-versions = "warn"

[sources]
# Crates come from crates.io and nowhere else, unless added to an allow list.
unknown-registry = "deny"
unknown-git = "deny"

newproj.Cargo.lock:
# This file is automatically @generated by Cargo.

version = 4

[[package]]
name = "retrying"
version = "0.1.0"

rust.Cargo.lock:
# This file is automatically @generated by Cargo.

[[package]]
name = "stock"
version = "0.1.0"
rust.Cargo.toml:
[package]
name = "stock"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.85"

[dependencies]

[lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"

[lints.clippy]
unwrap_used = "warn"
expect_used = "warn"
todo = "warn"
unimplemented = "warn"
dbg_macro = "warn"
clone_on_ref_ptr = "warn"
allow_attributes_without_reason = "warn"
rust.clippy.toml:
# Tests may unwrap: a panic there is a failed test, which is what you want.
allow-unwrap-in-tests = true
allow-expect-in-tests = true

explain.show: $ cargo clippy --explain unwrap_used    # the first lines
explain.out:
### What it does
Checks for `.unwrap()` or `.unwrap_err()` calls on `Result`s and `.unwrap()` call on `Option`s.

### Why restrict this?
It is better to handle the `None` or `Err` case,
or at least call `.expect(_)` with a more helpful message. Still, for a lot of
quick-and-dirty code, `unwrap` is a good choice, which is why this lint is
`Allow` by default.
